title: 8.9 An On-Cell Monitoring and Balancing System with Near-Field Communications for EV Batteries
problem: Battery management systems (BMS) for EVs and grid storage require per-cell monitoring and charge balancing with reliable contactless communication and robust network formation, but traditional wired monitoring scales poorly with cell count (up to 216 cells).
motivation: EV and grid-storage batteries demand timely fault detection and performance loss identification for safety and reliability; per-cell distributed processing enables localized balancing and reduces wiring complexity.
method: Each battery cell gets its own small monitoring chip (CM) that talks wirelessly to a central control unit (system hub, or SH) using serial communication—meaning data travels one bit at a time without physical wires. The chips measure each cell's voltage and charge state, then can rebalance charge across cells when needed. The wireless network adapts dynamically to reliably connect up to 216 monitoring chips to a single hub, eliminating the physical wiring normally required for large battery packs.
key_novelty: Wireless (contactless) serial communication for per-cell monitoring eliminates wiring while supporting the same monitoring chip design across different battery pack sizes.
contributions: Distributed per-cell monitor (CM) chip architecture with local processing and storage
Contactless serial communication protocol for SH-to-CM network with robust formation and recovery
Scalable architecture supporting up to 216 cell monitors per system hub
Cell reusability through generalized CM chip design independent of pack topology

metrics.other: Up to 216 cell monitors per system hub

baselines: Traditional wired BMS designs; conventional cell-level monitoring architectures
limitations: Power consumption, communication bandwidth, and latency specifications not discussed; temperature range and reliability under fault conditions not detailed.
primary_theme: Distributed contactless battery cell monitoring and balancing
